title: LLM4VV: Exploring LLM-as-a-Judge for Validation and Verification Testsuites
problem: LLM-generated compiler tests for directive-based parallel programming models (OpenMP, OpenACC) require validation to ensure correctness and reliability. The challenge is developing methods to assess whether LLMs can reliably judge the validity of generated compiler tests without understanding the 'black box' model internals.
motivation: LLMs show promise for generating software artifacts including compiler tests, but concerns about reliability, bias, and explainability require methods to validate and verify LLM-generated outputs in critical systems.
method: The authors employ an agent-based prompting approach to evaluate DeepSeek's deepseek-coder-33B-instruct model by challenging it with intentionally-erroneous code. They define evaluation metrics and implement a pipeline-based validation architecture that orchestrates the workflow for automatically validating LLM-generated compiler tests for OpenMP and OpenACC.
key_novelty: LLM-as-a-judge framework using agent-based prompting and pipeline validation to reliably assess and improve the quality of LLM-generated compiler tests for parallel programming models.
contributions: Agent-based prompting approach for evaluating LLM judgment of code correctness
Pipeline-based validation architecture for automating assessment of LLM-generated tests
Metrics and evaluation framework for probing LLM capabilities on compiler test generation
Empirical demonstration that structured validation significantly improves test quality assessment

metrics.accuracy: quality of LLM judgment on test correctness

limitations: Specific limitations and generalization to other LLM models not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: LLM-as-judge for automated compiler test validation
